update_log: Baseline initialization of high-frequency Indus Valley Civilization (Harappan) sites, their geographic locations, excavators, and key archaeological discoveries for History Static GK.

sites_in_present_day_pakistan.key_findings: The first IVC site to be discovered. Key finds include a row of 6 granaries, workmen's quarters, stone symbols of Lingam and Yoni, and a painted pottery.
Means 'Mound of the Dead'. Key finds include the Great Bath, the Great Granary, the Bronze Dancing Girl statue, the Steatite statue of a Bearded Priest, and the Pashupati Seal.
The only Indus city without a citadel. Famous as an industrial hub for bead-making factories, lipsticks, and a footprint of a dog chasing a cat.

sites_in_present_day_india.key_findings: The 'Manchester of IVC' and a major port city. Key finds include the world's earliest known artificial Dockyard, fire altars, rice husks, and double burial (male and female in a single grave).
Means 'Black Bangles'. Key finds include a ploughed field surface, fire altars, camel bones, and wooden drainage systems.

Recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2021. Unique for its 3-part city division (unlike the usual 2-part division) and a highly advanced water harnessing system/reservoirs. Found a large 10-letter signboard.
The only Indus site where actual bones of a horse were found, along with stone-covered burials.
Currently recognized as the largest Indus Valley Civilization site in the world (surpassing Mohenjo-Daro). Features a provincial capital status, granaries, and DNA-tested burials.
Notable for lacking a proper grid pattern for streets and lacking systematic drainage. Key finds include a terracotta replica of a toy plough and high-quality barley.
